statement: Show that the equation $\\mathrm{e}^{x}=3x$ has exactly two positive real roots, and find them correct to three decimal places.
solution: Let $f(x)=\\mathrm{e}^{x}-3x$. Then $f'(x)=\\mathrm{e}^{x}-3$, zero at $x=\\ln3\\approx1.099$, where $f(\\ln3)=3-3\\ln3\\approx-0.296<0$. Since $f(0)=1>0$ and $f(x)\\to\\infty$ as $x\\to\\infty$, $f$ has one root in $(0,\\ln3)$ and one in $(\\ln3,\\infty)$. Numerically: root$_1\\approx0.619$ (since $\\mathrm{e}^{0.619}\\approx1.857=3\\cdot0.619$), root$_2\\approx1.512$ (since $\\mathrm{e}^{1.512}\\approx4.536=3\\cdot1.512$).
hints: Use a numerical method near the two sign changes.
